wxFrame.scope: Native-backed CLOS construction, including subclass initargs/defaults and managed rollback. Title, width and height; parent is NULL, ID is wxID_ANY, remaining options use defaults. Full class and inherited API coverage remain open. Frame-only synchronous close requests now preserve veto/force semantics and native acceptance; no destruction guarantee.

wxPanel.scope: Native-backed CLOS construction, including subclass initargs/defaults and managed rollback. Parent only; remaining constructor options use defaults. Full class and inherited API coverage remain open.

wxButton.scope: Native-backed CLOS construction, including subclass initargs/defaults and managed rollback. Parent and label; ID is wxID_ANY, remaining options use defaults. Full class and inherited API coverage remain open.

wxTextCtrl.scope: Native-backed CLOS construction, including subclass initargs/defaults and managed rollback. Parent and initial value; ID is wxID_ANY, remaining options use defaults. Full class and inherited API coverage remain open.

wxStaticText.scope: Native-backed CLOS construction, including subclass initargs/defaults and managed rollback. Parent and label; ID is wxID_ANY, remaining options use defaults. Full class and inherited API coverage remain open.

wxCheckBox.scope: Native-backed CLOS construction, including subclass initargs/defaults and managed rollback. Parent, label and initial boolean value; two-state control, ID is wxID_ANY, remaining options use defaults. Full class and inherited API coverage remain open.

wxChoice.scope: Native-backed CLOS construction, including subclass initargs/defaults and managed rollback. Parent, copied strings and initial selection; wxArrayString overload, ID is wxID_ANY, remaining options use defaults. Full class and inherited API coverage remain open.

wxBoxSizer.scope: Parent-owned horizontal/vertical layout only; standalone sizers and full API remain open.

wxWindow.scope: Logical names, visibility and effective enabled state, layout, geometry and destruction are exposed; the remaining wxWindow API stays open. Managed handler stacks and explicit stack-aware copied routing are now supported. Push preserves bridge ownership; default pop/remove detach alive, deleting pop consumes native resource. All eight managed native widget destructors pop(false) before base teardown, independent of destroy observers/enabled flags. No external adoption/SetEventHandler or retained origins.

wxTopLevelWindow.scope: Canonical SETF writer. Title get/set is exposed for wxFrame only; other top-level types and the remaining top-level API stay open.

wxGauge.scope: Parent-owned progress gauge: positive range, value, horizontal/vertical orientation and pulsing. Constructor options, two-step creation and full inherited API remain open. Gauge support introduced in ABI 10; current bridge ABI 30; see docs/GAUGE.md and tests/gauge.lisp.

wxAppConsole.scope: Managed bridge application only: session lifetime, native main loop, polling, queued-event status/dispatch and callback/pump guards. No constructible application wrapper, application traits, arbitrary event loops, command-line hooks or native virtual overrides. Arbitrary native event classes and persistent mutable events, pushed-handler ownership, filters, propagation, idle handlers, timers and worker dispatch remain open. Borrowed managed application handler view supports inherited binding/dispatch/state; construction and explicit deletion reject. OS session delivery and native application subclass hooks remain unverified/unbound. Query/end-session binding is available on the managed app and isolated owned handlers; synthetic app/window session emission rejects; OS delivery remains unverified.

wxApp.scope: One managed GUI application per process on its main thread. Native initialization/cleanup only; application subclass hooks, traits, top-window APIs and remaining GUI-application interfaces are unbound. The CLOS APPLICATION-HANDLER is a borrowed event-handler view only. Borrowed managed application handler view supports inherited binding/dispatch/state; construction and explicit deletion reject. OS session delivery and native application subclass hooks remain unverified/unbound. Query/end-session binding is available on the managed app and isolated owned handlers; synthetic app/window session emission rejects; OS delivery remains unverified.

wxEvtHandler.scope: Managed standalone ownership, borrowed window/app identities, guarded standalone chains and managed window stacks support bindings, ID/range filters, normal/local/copied/pending/transfer delivery and bounded target cancellation. Handler-wide Lisp client data and distinct per-binding EQ USER-DATA use native numeric token adapters with session/frame/snapshot lifetime guards. Attached session delivery and dispatch-time structural edits reject. External adoption, arbitrary raw typed/untyped/userData/client/item pointers, generic container ownership, per-handler pending queries, app-wide cancellation, native OS-session validation, timer/idle and worker facilities remain open.

wxEvent.scope: Supported immutable snapshots, innermost native contexts and detached owned command/notify/close resources provide generic metadata/payload views, bounded registered-tag SETF, NIL-only origin clearing and native clone/copy/post/transfer semantics. Per-binding EQ Lisp USER-DATA is captured by snapshots and retained by active context frames across unbind; mutable referents are not deep-copied. Remaining gaps include arbitrary native classes/tags, retained or new origin objects, general native userData/client/item pointer adoption, generic wxObject wrappers and broader event families.

wxCloseEvent.scope: Supported close/session snapshots and scoped contexts, including checked veto and logging-off metadata. Native app bindings exist; real OS session delivery is unverified. Synthetic session queue/process requires isolated owned handlers and blocks wxApp fallback. No persistent event ownership or arbitrary close types. Timestamp/command classification snapshots and current reads, bounded native LONG timestamp SETF and close-only CanVeto SETF are implemented; snapshots stay immutable. Session-owned detached exact command/notify/close events now support native construction, cloning, disposal and copied dispatch; no arbitrary derived class, retained origin, client/userData ownership or arbitrary native transfer. Native wxEVT_TEXT payload guards prevent lazy text-entry origin shadowing; detached clones freeze effective strings. Supported owned events can now be transferred through wxQueueEvent after preflight; the original handle is consumed. Post/local operations preserve source through independent copies.

wxNotifyEvent.scope: Registered notify snapshots/current views and exact owned wxNotifyEvent resources provide payload metadata, Veto/Allow and guarded detached clone/copy/post/transfer operations. Shared per-binding EQ Lisp USER-DATA readers retain association lifetimes without adopting native pointers; handler client data remains separate. Native control-specific notify subclasses, broad virtual hooks, retained origins, general native client/item/userData pointer ownership and worker dispatch remain open.

wxCommandEvent.scope: Supported built-in/registered command snapshots, current views and exact owned base-class events provide counted UTF-8 text, signed32 integer, native LONG extra metadata and kind-limited checked/selection semantics. Detached cloning/copying/posting/transfer and bounded native-tag/origin operations preserve existing guards. Per-binding EQ Lisp USER-DATA is read through shared snapshot/context association APIs, not command client fields. Arbitrary derived control payload semantics, retained origins, native client/item/userData pointer adoption and worker dispatch remain open.

wxClientData.scope: Prerequisite native token-adapter subclass only for managed wxEvtHandler client objects, backed by session Lisp roots. Native adapter deletion invalidates association; asynchronous roots reap at access/cleanup/session end. No public wxClientData wrapper/factory, arbitrary subclasses, untyped/client/userData/item ownership or full container API.

wxObject.scope: Prerequisite entry-owned native binding-token adapter only; Lisp object retained separately by association/frame/snapshot references. No generic public wxObject wrapper/factory, raw pointer adoption, reference-data API or arbitrary ownership.
